data.one_liner: Lightweight and practical functional programming features for Dart.
data.what_it_does: Provides functional programming principles like Either, Result, and practical extensions for nullable types, iterables, and strings. It aims to stay aligned with the standard Dart workflow instead of deep hardcore FP features.
use_when: You want practical functional helpers like Either, Result, or nullable extensions in your codebase.
You prefer lightweight functional utilities over heavy or complex FP libraries.
avoid_when: You need deep and hardcore functional programming features (use dartz instead).
You do not use functional programming patterns in your project.
strengths: Lightweight and practical for production codebases.
Extensions for nullable types, strings, and iterables.
Aligns well with standard Dart idioms.
weaknesses: Some sections like Either documentation are still marked as TBD in the README.

alternatives.name: dartz
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick dartz if you need deep and hardcore functional programming features.
